definitions.explanation: Used as a modifier to indicate that an action, skill, or attitude is directed toward or involves other people. Almost always attached to another noun rather than standing alone.

examples.japanese: {対人|たいじん}{関係|かんけい}に{悩|なや}んでいる。
examples.english: I'm troubled by my interpersonal relationships.

examples.japanese: {対人|たいじん}スキルを{磨|みが}くことが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It is important to polish your interpersonal skills.

examples.japanese: {自動車|じどうしゃ}{保険|ほけん}には、{対人|たいじん}{賠償|ばいしょう}と{対物|たいぶつ}{賠償|ばいしょう}がある。
examples.english: Car insurance includes both personal liability and property liability coverage.

notes:
Functions as a modifier prefix combining {対|たい} (toward, against) + {人|じん} (person). Always paired with a following noun.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {対人|たいじん}{関係|かんけい}: interpersonal relationships
- {対人|たいじん}スキル: interpersonal skills
- {対人|たいじん}{恐怖症|きょうふしょう}: social anxiety; fear of people
- {対人|たいじん}{賠償|ばいしょう}: personal liability (insurance)
- {対人|たいじん}{援助|えんじょ}: helping/support work

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {対物|たいぶつ}: toward objects — its counterpart, used especially in insurance
- {人間|にんげん}{関係|かんけい}: human relationships — more general; can replace {対人|たいじん}{関係|かんけい} in casual speech
